guideTitle: 6 Best Hose Reels and Carts for Pressure Washers in 2026
metaDescription: Six pressure washer hose reels and carts compared on hose length, PSI rating, mounting style and auto-retract, so a long high-pressure hose stops tangling.
introParagraphs: A garden hose reel cart is the wrong tool for a pressure washer. High-pressure hose is stiff, narrow and rated by PSI, and it needs a reel built for that diameter and for fittings that will not fail under load. The good news is that a pressure washer reel can make a messy driveway job feel tidy, whether it rolls with the machine, bolts to a wall or mounts on a truck.

This lineup covers six options. The Active is an actual cart with 10 inch wheels and a built-in 100 foot reel for its own pressure washers, the M MINGLE holds 150 feet of 3/8 inch hose, the MEKOH holds 100 feet and carries a 4500 PSI rating, the YEHERIT mounts directly to a washer with four quick-release pins, the Giraffe Tools offers 65 feet with automatic rewind, and the VEVOR is a compact 50 foot bracket-mounted reel. Most are reels rather than rolling carts, and we say so on each pick.

We evaluated each one based on product specs and buyer feedback, concentrating on hose length and diameter, PSI rating, mounting style and winding method. Check your washer's hose diameter and thread before you buy, since compatibility is the most common reason these get returned.

products.name: Active 100 ft Pressure Washer Cart and Hose Reel
products.description:
The Active is the only true rolling cart in this lineup. It carries your whole pressure washer system on one stable base platform, with a built-in reel that winds up to 100 feet of 3/8 inch rubber pressure hose, or the same length of 5/16 or 1/4 inch hose. The carbon steel frame rides on 10 inch wheels, and the listing says it fits Active 2.0 and 2.3 washers and includes a jumper hose.

The two-position rotary handle locks upright for rolling and drops flat for storage, which is a thoughtful design for a bulky load. An integrated nylon net bin secures the nozzles, trigger gun, lance and foam cannon, and a secure lock stops the hose unspooling while you move. The listing says the pre-drilled platform fits every Active model and accommodates other standard units, but fit is the main thing to confirm if you own another brand. The excerpt also gives no PSI rating for the reel itself.

A two-year warranty backs the cart, and rolling the whole system to a work site is the real benefit over a wall-mounted reel. Check that your washer's footprint matches the pre-drilled holes before you buy. Compared with the YEHERIT, which mounts onto a washer, the Active gives you a wheeled base. Compared with the MEKOH at 100 feet of 3/8 inch hose, it holds the same length but adds wheels, a bin and a platform for the machine.
products.bestFor: Owners of Active 2.0 or 2.3 washers who want to roll everything at once.
pros: True rolling cart with 10 inch wheels
cons: PSI rating not stated for the reel

products.name: M MINGLE 150 ft Pressure Washer Hose Reel
specs: 150 ft of 3/8 inch or 300 ft of 1/4 inch

specList.label: Capacity
specList.value: 150 ft of 3/8 inch or 300 ft of 1/4 inch

products.description:
The M MINGLE offers the longest capacity here, 150 feet of 3/8 inch hose or 300 feet of 1/4 inch hose, with the hose not included. The frame is heavy gauge industrial steel with a corrosion-resistant powder coating and a full-flow solid swivel joint inlet. The listing gives a maximum of 4000 PSI and 176 degrees Fahrenheit with 3/8 inch NPT threads, and an 80 inch inlet pressure hose is included.

A direct hand-crank rewind with a swivel and smooth round handle puts the hose away, and a brass swivel with a stainless steel stem helps stop tangling. A 90-degree elbow preserves hose life. The bracket can be bolted by the base to a wall, workbench or any flat surface, or mounted to a pressure washer frame, and a quick-removal pin lock lets you detach it for portability. The tradeoff is that it is a mounted reel, not a cart, and 150 feet of hose adds noticeable weight to the mount point.

The listing warns that the pressure rating of your washer hose should stay below 4000 PSI to avoid damaging the reel, so check your machine before you buy. Confirm every connection from the washer inlet to the gun outlet before you start. Compared with the Active, it gives 50 more feet of 3/8 inch hose but no wheels. Compared with the MEKOH at 100 feet and 4500 PSI, it holds more hose but carries a lower pressure rating.
products.bestFor: Large driveways and workshops that need up to 150 feet of reach.

products.name: MEKOH 100 ft Heavy Duty Pressure Washer Hose Reel 4500 PSI
specs: 100 ft of 3/8 inch or 200 ft of 1/4 inch

specList.label: Capacity
specList.value: 100 ft of 3/8 inch or 200 ft of 1/4 inch

products.description:
The MEKOH 100 foot model is rated for 4500 PSI, the highest stated pressure in this group, and holds 100 feet of 3/8 inch hose or 200 feet of 1/4 inch hose. Its low-profile outlet and open drum allow smooth, unrestricted wrapping without the large bends traditional reels require. The solid steel U frame, ribbed edges and CNC spun disks suit home, commercial and industrial use.

The no-bend outlet is the standout detail, since sharp bends are where pressure hoses fail early, and the listing notes that a right-angle elbow can reduce flow by up to 25 percent with low-flow setups. An adjustable tension brake controls unwinding speed and prevents tangles, and the extended hand crank has a rounded grip. The tradeoff is that it is a mounted reel rather than a cart, and at 100 feet it holds less than the M MINGLE's 150 feet.

The package includes mounting hardware, an M22 adapter and Teflon tape, and the inlet and outlet use 3/8 inch female fittings. Check that your hose and fittings match before drilling. Compared with the YEHERIT at 4000 PSI, it has a higher stated rating and a tension brake. Compared with the Giraffe Tools at 65 feet and 3200 PSI, it uses a manual crank but handles far more pressure and hose.
products.bestFor: Owners of high-pressure washers who want a clear PSI rating and gentler hose bends.
cons: Holds less than the M MINGLE

products.name: YEHERIT 100 ft Pressure Washer Hose Reel 4000 PSI

specList.label: Mounting
specList.value: Fixed iron plate with 4 quick-release pins

products.description:
The YEHERIT is a heavy-duty steel reel with corrosion-resistant powder coating, rated for 4000 PSI and 100 feet of 3/8 inch hose. A fixed iron plate, matching hardware and four quick-release pin locks let it mount stably on a pressure washer, workbench, wall, van or trailer. A 360 degree swivel arm helps put the hose away quickly without kinks.

The listing says every part is detachable for quick disassembly and compact storage, with a complete setup in under 10 minutes. It uses 3/8 inch NPT male and M22 female fittings, so it connects to most hoses and pumps without adapters. That makes it practical if you move the reel between machines. The tradeoff is that it attaches to a washer or surface rather than rolling on its own, and the 4000 PSI rating is lower than the MEKOH's 4500.

Quick-release pins save time during setup, and the powder coating helps against rust on a wet driveway. Confirm that your washer frame can accept the iron plate before you buy. Compared with the M MINGLE at 150 feet, it is more portable but holds 50 feet less. Compared with the Active, it mounts on your existing washer instead of replacing the base, and it has no wheels or accessory bin.
products.bestFor: Owners who want to mount a reel on their existing washer quickly.
cons: Lower PSI rating than the MEKOH

products.name: Giraffe Tools 65 ft Auto-Rewind Pressure Washer Hose Reel
products.description:
The Giraffe Tools reel offers automatic rewind: you lock the 65 foot pressure hose at any length during use, and a gentle tug activates instant retraction. Four non-snag rollers keep retraction smooth and prevent kinks and tangles. Wall or floor brackets are included, and it can be installed vertically or horizontally in a wall, ceiling or floor spot. The listing gives a 3200 PSI rating and a 150 degree Fahrenheit limit.

Auto-retract is the most comfortable winding method for people with limited hand strength, since there is no cranking at all. An adjustable reinforced stainless steel guide arm optimizes hose alignment, and a self-adjusting stop ball and anti-abrasion design protect the hose. The tradeoff is capacity and pressure, since 65 feet is the shortest here after the 50 foot VEVOR and 3200 PSI is the lowest stated rating. It also needs a mount, so it is not rolling, and spring-driven reels require a firm tug to hold or release.

A 24-month warranty covers the reel, and the heavy-duty steel frame resists rust and UV damage. Install it near the washer on a stud or masonry surface, and confirm all connections before use. Compared with the VEVOR at 50 feet, it gives 15 more feet of reach plus auto-rewind. Compared with the MEKOH at 4500 PSI, it suits lighter machines and hands that prefer no crank.
products.bestFor: Garages with a modest washer where cranking is a hassle.
pros: Automatic rewind with lock at any length
Flexible wall, ceiling or floor mounting
cons: 3200 PSI is the lowest rating here

products.name: VEVOR 50 ft x 3/8 Inch Pressure Washer Hose Reel
products.description:
The VEVOR is a compact 50 foot reel with a heavy-duty steel bracket that mounts on a wall, floor or truck. A comfort grip handle makes hose retrieval easy, and a locking ring keeps the hose in place during use. The 90-degree swivel inlet is solid brass, which is leak-proof and corrosion resistant. The listing gives 4000 PSI maximum, 176 degrees Fahrenheit and an M22 connector, and a 6.6 foot lead-in hose is included.

It is the simplest and smallest option here, which suits tight workshops or truck beds. The locking ring prevents the hose from creeping out, and the brass inlet is a real durability advantage. The tradeoff is length, since 50 feet will limit reach on bigger jobs, it is a mounted reel and not a cart, and manual cranking takes effort for a full length.

The bracket needs a solid mounting surface, and the listing says it supports 3/8 inch hose up to 50 feet. Because the 4000 PSI rating matches the YEHERIT and M MINGLE, it is not a weak link for most home washers. Compared with the Giraffe Tools at 65 feet, it holds less and is manual but has a higher pressure rating. Compared with the M MINGLE at 150 feet, it is much shorter and lighter, which suits small spaces and mobile setups.
products.bestFor: Tight workshops and truck mounts where a compact reel fits best.
pros: Mounts on wall, floor or truck
cons: Manual crank for a full length

buyingCriteria.explanation: Pressure hose is narrow and stiff, so capacity depends on diameter. The M MINGLE holds 150 feet of 3/8 inch or 300 feet of 1/4 inch hose, the MEKOH 100 foot model and YEHERIT hold 100 feet of 3/8 inch, the Giraffe Tools holds 65 feet and the VEVOR 50. Check your washer's hose diameter first, and note that thinner hose stores more length but delivers less flow. A reel rated for one diameter will not take a thicker one.

The reel must handle your washer's pressure. The MEKOH 100 foot model is rated for 4500 PSI, the YEHERIT, M MINGLE and VEVOR for 4000, and the Giraffe Tools for 3200. Pick a rating at or above your washer's maximum, and note that the M MINGLE listing asks that your washer hose stay below 4000 PSI. Cheap fittings are a safety risk at high pressure.

Reels either mount to a wall or floor, attach to a washer, or ride on a cart. The M MINGLE and VEVOR bolt down, the YEHERIT and M MINGLE can mount to a washer frame with pin locks, and the Active rolls on 10 inch wheels. Decide where the reel will live before choosing. A bolted reel is stable but fixed, so use fasteners suited to your wall or floor.

Manual cranks save money and spring reels save effort. The Giraffe Tools rewinds automatically and locks at any length, while the M MINGLE, MEKOH, YEHERIT and VEVOR use hand cranks, and the MEKOH adds a tension brake. Cranking 100 feet of hose is a workout. Choose auto-retract if grip strength is limited, and a tension brake if you dislike hose tangles.

Sharp bends kill pressure hose early. The MEKOH uses a low-profile outlet to avoid large bends, the VEVOR and M MINGLE use 90-degree brass swivel inlets, and the YEHERIT has a 360 degree swivel arm. Brass fittings resist corrosion and leaks. Check thread type, such as 3/8 inch NPT on the YEHERIT and M22 on several, against your washer.

These reels are not universal. The Active is built around Active 2.0 and 2.3 washers with a pre-drilled platform and a jumper hose, while others need you to match threads and hose. The MEKOH ships with an M22 adapter and the VEVOR includes a 6.6 foot lead-in hose. Read the compatibility notes before buying, because a reel that does not fit your hose is useless.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and diameter
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated hose lengths and diameters. The M MINGLE leads with 150 feet of 3/8 inch hose. The Active, MEKOH and YEHERIT hold 100 feet, the Giraffe Tools holds 65 and the VEVOR 50. Reels that list two diameters scored for flexibility.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pressure rating
howWeEvaluated.description: We used stated PSI ratings only. The MEKOH lists 4500, the YEHERIT, M MINGLE and VEVOR 4000, and the Giraffe Tools 3200. The Active listing gives no rating for the reel, which we noted rather than assumed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mounting and mobility
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each installs. The Active rolls on 10 inch wheels, the YEHERIT and M MINGLE pin to a washer or bolt down, and the VEVOR bolts to a wall, floor or truck. The Giraffe Tools mounts on a wall, ceiling or floor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rewind and hose care
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed winding method and bend control. The Giraffe Tools offers auto-retract with four non-snag rollers, the MEKOH avoids sharp bends and has a tension brake, and the VEVOR and M MINGLE use brass 90-degree swivels.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and value
howWeEvaluated.description: Steel gauge and finishes were checked. The M MINGLE uses heavy gauge industrial steel, the YEHERIT and Giraffe Tools use powder-coated steel, and the Active carries a two-year warranty. Lineup positioning runs from the Active as the only rolling cart to the VEVOR as the most compact.

faq.q: Can I use a garden hose reel cart for a pressure washer?
faq.a: Generally no. Pressure hose is narrower and stiffer and needs fittings rated for PSI. Use a reel designed for pressure hose such as the MEKOH or YEHERIT, and match its 3/8 inch NPT or M22 fittings to your washer.

Match or exceed your washer's maximum. The MEKOH 100 foot model is rated 4500 PSI, the YEHERIT, M MINGLE and VEVOR 4000, and the Giraffe Tools 3200. Check your washer's manual, and remember the hose and fittings must also be rated high enough.

faq.q: How much hose will it hold?
faq.a: The M MINGLE holds 150 feet of 3/8 inch hose, the MEKOH and YEHERIT hold 100 feet, the Giraffe Tools 65 and the VEVOR 50. Thinner 1/4 inch hose stores more, up to 300 feet on the M MINGLE. A full reel adds weight to the mount.

Usually not. The M MINGLE states hose is not included, though it ships with an 80 inch inlet hose, and the Active includes a jumper hose. The VEVOR includes a 6.6 foot lead-in hose. Check each listing.
Sharp bends and abrasion shorten hose life. The MEKOH uses a low-profile outlet and the VEVOR uses a brass 90-degree swivel. Avoid kinking and never wind hose under strain.
Near the washer on a solid surface. The M MINGLE and VEVOR bolt down, and the Giraffe Tools mounts on walls, ceilings or floors. Use the right fasteners for your surface, since a full hose is heavy.

faq.q: Does hot water matter for these reels?
faq.a: Yes. The M MINGLE and VEVOR list 176 degrees Fahrenheit, the Giraffe Tools 150, and the MEKOH 50 foot model 225. Check your washer's water temperature limit before you connect it, and never run a hot-water machine through a reel with a lower rating.
